prompt: On a certain day, $1$ US dollar is worth $1.25$ Canadian dollars. How many US dollars are equivalent to $400$ Canadian dollars?
hint: Before computing, decide whether the number of US dollars should be larger or smaller than $400$. That tells you which operation to use.

hints.text: Before computing, decide whether the number of US dollars should be larger or smaller than $400$. That tells you which operation to use.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try an easy rate: if $1$ USD $= 2$ CAD, then $10$ CAD is clearly $5$ USD — you divide. Decide bigger-or-smaller first, and the operation follows.
One US dollar buys more than one Canadian dollar, so fewer US dollars are needed. Divide the Canadian amount by the rate: $400 \div 1.25$.
Since $400 \div 1.25 = 320$, the amount is $320$ US dollars.

learningObjective: Convert between currencies, choosing the correct direction.
explanation: The exchange rate says that $1$ US dollar equals $1.25$ Canadian dollars.
To change Canadian dollars into US dollars, divide by $1.25$ so the Canadian units cancel: $400 \div 1.25 = 320$.
The answer is smaller than $400$, as expected, so $400$ Canadian dollars equal $320$ US dollars.

alternativeExplanations.title: Estimate the direction first
steps: One US dollar buys more than one Canadian dollar, so any pile of money is a *smaller* number when counted in US dollars.
That single sentence tells you to divide, before you touch the arithmetic.
On every conversion question, predicting bigger-or-smaller first eliminates the multiply/divide coin flip.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Multiplying gives 500 — more US dollars than Canadian, from the stronger currency. That direction is impossible.
Decide bigger-or-smaller before any arithmetic: the US amount must be the smaller number, so divide by 1.25.
